problem.title: Fixing Redis Fork Copy-on-Write Memory Bloat
problem.prompt: A production Redis 7 primary holds a 24 GB dataset on a 32 GB RAM Linux host and handles 15,000 writes/sec (each mutating ~64 bytes across random keys). Whenever an hourly `BGSAVE` RDB snapshot (taking 90 seconds) or `BGREWRITEAOF` triggers `fork()`, the child process shares pages with the parent via Copy-on-Write (CoW). Within 70 seconds of `fork()`, Redis RSS balloons from 24 GB to >31.5 GB and the Linux kernel OOM-kills the Redis primary. Inspection shows Transparent Huge Pages (THP) is set to `always`. Design the OS memory, Redis persistence, and automated CoW-guardrail architecture to prevent OOM kills while preserving durable backups.

spark.summary: When Linux Transparent Huge Pages (2 MB) is enabled, a 64-byte write during Redis BGSAVE fork() copies an entire 2 MB page (512x write amplification), doubling RSS from 24 GB to 48 GB in 90 seconds and triggering the OOM killer.
spark.keyTakeaway: Disable Transparent Huge Pages (`echo never > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled`), cap Redis `maxmemory` at <= 55% of host RAM, monitor `rdb_last_cow_size`, and gate BGSAVE during heavy write bursts.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** When Redis runs `BGSAVE` or `BGREWRITEAOF`, `fork()` shares memory pages with the child via Copy-on-Write (CoW). Under standard `4 KB` Linux pages, `15,000` random 64-byte writes/sec over 90s dirties at most `~5.4 GB`.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts 2 MB Hugepages Turn 24 GB BGSAVE into OOM Kill in 70s (15k Writes/s -> Redis Primary (24GB) -> Linux CoW + THP -> BGSAVE Child); THP=never (4 KB CoW) + Replica Snapshot Offload (15k Random Writes/s -> Primary (maxmemory <=55%) -> Async Replication Stream -> Backup Replica (BGSAVE)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Running a `fork()`-enabled Redis primary at `75%–85%` of host RAM leaves less than `25%` headroom for normal `4 KB` CoW overhead, replica output buffers, and jemalloc fragmentation. Guarantee `used_memory + CoW_overhead <= 85%` of 32 GB RAM during 90-second snapshots: **Permanently Disable THP**: Set `transparent_hugepage=never` in kernel boot args / systemd.

**Failure Modes & Application:** OS page-table and CoW mechanics apply to all fork-based persistence engines: **Production Redis / Valkey Clusters**: Standardize `THP=never`, `vm.overcommit_memory=1`, and `50–55%` memory caps.

learningJourney.title: Why Linux Transparent Huge Pages amplify Redis fork() memory by 512x
learningJourney.explanation: When Redis runs `BGSAVE` or `BGREWRITEAOF`, `fork()` shares memory pages with the child via Copy-on-Write (CoW). Under standard `4 KB` Linux pages, `15,000` random 64-byte writes/sec over 90s dirties at most `~5.4 GB`. With **2 MB Transparent Huge Pages (THP)** enabled, each 64-byte write forces the kernel to copy an entire `2 MB` page—**512x write amplification**.

learningJourney.title: RSS doubling from 24 GB to 48 GB and Linux OOM kills
learningJourney.explanation:
On a 32 GB host holding a 24 GB dataset (75% RAM), `BGSAVE` with THP enabled causes two catastrophic failures:

1. **OOM Kill in 70 Seconds**: Random writes dirty `2 MB` hugepages until RSS climbs past 32 GB (toward 48 GB), triggering the Linux OOM killer.
2. **20–50 ms `fork()` Stalls**: Allocating and compacting hugepage tables (`khugepaged`) stalls the main `aeMain` thread.

learningJourney.title: Why setting maxmemory to 85% or transient sysfs edits fail
learningJourney.explanation: Running a `fork()`-enabled Redis primary at `75%–85%` of host RAM leaves less than `25%` headroom for normal `4 KB` CoW overhead, replica output buffers, and jemalloc fragmentation. Moreover, running `echo never > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled` without persisting it in systemd/GRUB reverts silently on the next host reboot.

learningJourney.title: Enterprise solution: Disable THP, Cap maxmemory <= 55%, and Offload BGSAVE
learningJourney.explanation:
Guarantee `used_memory + CoW_overhead <= 85%` of 32 GB RAM during 90-second snapshots:

- **Permanently Disable THP**: Set `transparent_hugepage=never` in kernel boot args / systemd unit (`enabled` and `defrag`), cutting CoW page size from `2 MB` to `4 KB`.
- **Cap `maxmemory <= 55%` (~17.6 GB)**: Reserves `~14.4 GB` for `5.4 GB` worst-case 4 KB CoW, replication buffers, and OS page cache.
- **Offload `BGSAVE` to a Dedicated Replica**: Disable `save` on the primary and run RDB/AOF snapshots on a read replica, monitoring `rdb_last_cow_size`.

cards.detail: Never exceed 55% maxmemory on any node that calls fork() for RDB, AOF, or full resync.

cards.label: Monitor rdb_last_cow_size

learningJourney.title: Where fork() CoW sizing governs stateful infrastructure
learningJourney.explanation:
OS page-table and CoW mechanics apply to all fork-based persistence engines:

- **Production Redis / Valkey Clusters**: Standardize `THP=never`, `vm.overcommit_memory=1`, and `50–55%` memory caps.
- **Managed Cache Services (ElastiCache / Memorystore)**: Reserve `reserved-memory-percent` (`25–45%`) specifically for `BGSAVE` and failover syncs.
- **High-Write AOF Compaction**: Gate `BGREWRITEAOF` during peak traffic windows.

_nextProblem.title: Building Reliable Change Data Capture (CDC) Pipelines
_nextProblem.prompt: A Debezium PostgreSQL connector (`pgoutput`) streams 8,500 writes/sec from an `orders` database to Kafka, feeding Elasticsearch and Snowflake. After a Kafka broker disk failure and an accidental `DROP_REPLICATION_SLOT` during disk-full remediation, the connector restarts with missing offsets in `connect-offsets`. Because `snapshot.mode=when_needed` was set without `heartbeat.interval.ms` on a low-write-table slot, 4 hours of `orders` updates (1.2M rows) are silently skipped, and Elasticsearch returns stale order statuses to customers. Design a fault-tolerant Debezium CDC pipeline that prevents offset/LSN loss, detects gaps automatically, and repairs missed rows without full-table locks.

options.explanation: Read-Your-Writes ensures a client always observes its own completed writes.
The write was durable on the primary; the replica simply lagged.
Atomicity governs all-or-nothing commit, not cross-replica visibility.

options.explanation: BPE still tokenizes the text normally.

options.text: It invalidates prefix/KV caching for all subsequent 3,000 tokens on every request
options.explanation: Correct! Prefix KV caching requires an exact token match from index 0 onward.
Output length is unaffected; Prefill cache reuse is what breaks.
